title: World Cup Ticket Disaster: Fans Left Outside Stadiums
summary: Imagine saving up your allowance for months to buy something really cool, and then it never arrives. That's what happened to some World Cup fans. John McNicholas, 65, drove four hours from New Jersey to Boston with his friend from England. He spent over $1,200 on two tickets. But when they got to the stadium, the tickets were gone — just vanished from his account. They stood outside listening to the cheers inside, hoping until halftime. But nothing. Brad Michel spent $15,600 on three tickets for a game in Houston. He wanted to take his 12-year-old son and his wife's dad from Sweden. The tickets never came. StubHub offered him worse seats, but he said no. They watched the game on TV at their Airbnb. Brett Romas flew from Canada to Houston with his 13-year-old son, a huge fan of soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo. StubHub sent him tickets for the wrong game in the wrong city. He got a refund, but no game. StubHub says the problem is FIFA's app. FIFA says only tickets bought from them are guaranteed. Who's right? The fans just want to see the game.
why_it_matters: This shows how important it is to buy from trusted sources and to be careful when buying things online, because even big companies can make mistakes.

background_read: The World Cup is a huge soccer tournament held every four years, run by FIFA (the world soccer organization).
Fans often buy tickets from resale websites like StubHub, but digital tickets can disappear if apps have technical problems.
Sometimes the official seller and the reseller blame each other, leaving fans without a way to get in.
Article_Structure: WHO: Three fans: John McNicholas, Brad Michel, and Brett Romas.
WHAT: They bought tickets to World Cup games but were left outside because the tickets were missing or wrong.
WHERE: Stadiums in Boston and Houston.
WHY: StubHub and FIFA each blame the other, and fans are caught in the middle without a solution.

perspectives.description: Fans are angry and disappointed because they lost money and missed a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
StubHub says the problem is FIFA's app, not their own website, so they feel it is not their fault.
FIFA says only tickets bought directly from them are guaranteed, meaning fans who use resellers take a big risk.
